chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: The Nest Club routine and a lead-sheet overcoat
summary: The six-piece band worked 10 to 8 at the unlicensed Nest Club, run by Mal Frazier and Johnny Carey, and Danny bought a full orchestration of an overcoat for his first winter.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: An after-hour club. It wasn't exactly an after-hours spot. It didn't have a license. The bosses were Mal Frazier and Johnny Carey, and they were all, um, sweetie-pies... Because all they did was, a whole lot of women came through there. It must have been an assignation joint, where you send out chicks to hustle. Because they had these all these glamour, supposedly glamour women coming to...

We were going into Fall. It was the month of October, and it's cold, beginning to get cold. I had never actually been in snow. I saw it from a train going from Chicago to New Orleans. I saw it, but I had never been in snow. I was waiting for the snow. I had bought my overcoat. It wasn't a lead sheet, because there was a difference between an overcoat and a lead sheet. They would tell you if you had one of those little flimsy coats in New York, "Hey, you'd better get rid of that... Hawk is comin' through here. You'd better get rid of that lead sheet and get you a full orchestration."

All right. So I worked at night at the Nest Club. And you go to work at ten, you sit on the bandstand, and you look. You don't say much, because the action starts maybe around two. You went in there with the specifications and the agreement that you stayed until the last customer went out. Then you could make money. It was noted that you got tips and you could expect tips, and the entertainer split with you. It was a hustle for everybody, so you agreed to stay in there maybe until eight o'clock in the morning -- as long as they had people. That was the (?).
